Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testLocaleIndependence` is designed to ensure that encoding with Soundex is locale-independent. It encodes input strings under different locales (English, Turkish, and the system default) and compares their encoded results to verify consistency.

The failure indicates that the Soundex encoding is dependent on the system locale, which violates the expectation of consistent results regardless of locale.

Examining the code snippet for `Soundex.encode(String)` reveals it calls the `soundex(String)` method. This method processes the string after cleaning it via `SoundexUtils.clean(String)`.

Looking at `SoundexUtils.clean(String)`, the input string is filtered to only letters and then converted to uppercase. Critically, the method calls toUpperCase() without specifying locale if all characters are letters (line 53), which means it uses the default locale. If the string had non-letter characters removed, it uses `toUpperCase(Locale.ENGLISH)` (line 55).

This asymmetry is the root cause of the locale-dependent behavior: when the entire string consists of letters, the conversion to uppercase uses the default locale, which can cause characters like 'i' to be converted differently in languages such as Turkish.

Inside `Soundex.map(char)`, the character `ch - 'A'` lookup depends on the uppercase character. If uppercase mapping differs per locale (especially with Turkish i-dotless and dotted i), it leads to inconsistent soundex code generation.

Hence, the root cause is the locale-dependent uppercase conversion in `SoundexUtils.clean(String)` on line 53, where `str.toUpperCase()` uses the default locale instead of a fixed locale (such as Locale.ENGLISH).

This explains why the test fails for different locales and why the Soundex language codec is platform-dependent as stated in the bug report's description.

In conclusion, the bug arises from improper case-insensitive string handling caused by locale-dependent uppercase conversion in `SoundexUtils.clean`, resulting in discrepancies between expected and actual soundex codes across locales.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
